analyses.predicted_outcome: Preregistered directions come from earlier Gemini-3-Flash / 512 px phases (this board is Gemini 3 at 384 px): H6 (Phase 4, the only untested confirmatory hypothesis) expected the stronger Pro model to transfer/match-or-exceed Flash; H7 (Phase 2b) found T=0.0 optimal for both tracks; H1 (Phase 2a) planned a text-only vs image-using contrast without a committed directional winner. Board result (genuine Pro, all Pro cells n>=3): H6 holds strongly and uniformly -- the top six cells are all genuine Pro, every Pro-text cell beats the best Flash cell (flash-image-minimal-t-0-0, F1 0.600), and the genuine Pro-image cells match Flash on F1 while dominating MCC (any apparent Flash-over-Pro in the raw board traces to the E57 Flash-misdispatched cells, now replaced). H7's T=0.0 optimum is cleanly supported within Pro text: the two Tier-1 cells are both T=0.0 (HIGH and MEDIUM thinking, tied) and the two Tier-2 cells are both T=0.7 -- a clear T=0.0 > T=0.7 ordering at matched model/modality. H1 resolves metric-dependently -- text wins F1@20 m localisation (the top four cells are all text) while image wins MCC tile-discrimination (pro-image-medium-t-0-7, MCC +0.911).
analyses.outcome: At the preregistered 20 m buffer the best single pass for mound localisation is genuine Gemini 3 Pro text at T=0.0. Tier 1 -- the tie_set -- is a two-member statistical tie between pro-text-high-t-0-0 (F1 0.804) and pro-text-medium-t-0-0 (F1 0.792): a round-robin tile-swap permutation (BH-FDR q=0.05; 129/153 pairs significant -> 7 tiers) cannot separate them, and both are significantly clear of the Tier-2 pair -- the two Pro-text T=0.7 cells, pro-text-medium-t-0-7 (0.755) and pro-text-high-t-0-7 (0.745). So at T=0.0 the thinking level (HIGH vs MEDIUM) does not significantly matter, and T=0.0 beats T=0.7 (Tier 1 vs Tier 2) at matched model and modality (H7). The top four cells are all Pro text and the top six all genuine Pro; the text-over-image advantage holds at matched settings (best Pro text 0.804 vs best Pro image 0.666). The F1 leaders are NOT the tile-level discrimination (MCC) leader: genuine Pro IMAGE wins MCC -- pro-image-medium-t-0-7 (MCC +0.911, but 9th on F1) and pro-image-high-t-0-0 (+0.868) -- while Pro text leads F1, so the best single-pass configuration is metric-dependent. (All eight Pro cells are genuine Gemini 3 Pro at n>=3; see deviations E57 and docs/methodology/n1-baseline-matrix.md for board provenance.) analyses.outcome: Both named claims of the diversity-dividend test hold at the preregistered 20m buffer — claim (2), consensus vs single-pass, is the registered H3 comparison (confirmed); claim (1), the thinking-level diversity dividend, is a POST-REGISTRATION (post-hoc) discovery: the registration fixes thinking_level=minimal (osf:1211-1212, 2135) and no erratum makes it a registered factor (D17 sweep U5; fence applied at the S134 PI walk). Per the registered H3 analysis plan (osf/preregistration.md:519-521: 'Compare single-pass mean F1 vs voted F1 at each (N, threshold) combination' + 'Generate threshold sweep curves' + 'Identify optimal (N, threshold)'), the headline is each configuration's BEST (N, threshold) operating point against the known test-tile ground truth -- the study's purpose is to characterise how well VLM symbol extraction localises mounds, so best-achievable performance is the deliverable, not a confound. Method: round-robin tile-swap permutation (10k perms, seed 42, two-sided; BH-FDR q=0.05) + greedy-clique tiering over a 22-cell board (4 consensus champions + 18 single-pass cells); 197/231 pairs significant -> 7 tiers. (1) DIVERSITY DIVIDEND (post-hoc; unregistered thinking factor) -- HIGH-thinking consensus significantly exceeds minimal-thinking consensus at matched modality: text +0.153 F1 (BH-p<0.001; MCC +0.239) and image +0.070 F1 (BH-p<0.001; MCC +0.272). The HIGH-thinking pools take the larger consensus gain -- more varied proposals let a high vote threshold prune their false positives. (2) CONSENSUS vs SINGLE-PASS -- every consensus champion significantly beats its matched within-pool single-pass baseline (+0.13 to +0.43 F1, all BH-p<0.001), and the lift persists at the production N=5 operating point (text 4-of-5, image 3-of-5; +0.09 to +0.33 F1). (3) CROSS-ARCHITECTURE HEADLINE -- Tier 1 (the tie_set) is a THREE-member statistical tie: the best Flash HIGH-text consensus (F1 0.814) and the two genuine-Gemini-3-Pro single-pass text leaders (pro-text-high-t-0-0 0.804, pro-text-medium-t-0-0 0.792); the permutation cannot separate Flash-consensus from the Pro leader (p=0.616, BH-p=0.66). Cheap Flash consensus reaches the expensive Pro single-pass tier on localisation F1. OPERATING-POINT SENSITIVITY (characterised, co-headlined): the Tier-1 parity is at the best (N, threshold) point (26-of-30); at the production N=5 carry-forward point (text 4-of-5) the same pool reaches TIER 2 (0.720), tying genuine Pro text at T=0.7 -- a best-minus-N5 delta of ~0.094 F1 (the within-test cousin of the carry-forward-vs-best delta the 55-map generalisation reports). F1-parity is NOT MCC-parity: the Pro text leaders are more tile-precise (MCC 0.790, 11 tile FPs) than the Flash consensus champion (MCC 0.620, 41 tile FPs) -- the metric-dependent-winner pattern of the n1 board persists. Deployment generalisation to unseen maps is the separate question answered by the 55-map runs. Era-2 487-tile test scope, 384px, gemini-3-flash. That comparison scored a 240-tile T=1.0 arm (outputs/h11/consensus-384-UNINTENDED-T1.0) against 487-tile bounds, charging 193 of 435 in-bounds ground-truth mounds to it as automatic false negatives (recall ceiling 0.5563). analyses.outcome: At matched 487-tile scope the E43 temperature effect does not survive: the four paired F1 permutation tests are all non-significant and all four point estimates favour T=1.0 (ΔF1 −0.021 p=0.335 and −0.020 p=0.358 at N=5 for 20 m / 30 m; −0.034 p=0.082 and −0.032 p=0.096 at N=10), against the +0.168 to +0.194 (p=0.0) reported by the confounded group_4 tests. Tile-level MCC points the same way and more strongly: 0.3148 vs 0.4065 at N=5 and 0.3655 vs 0.4153 at N=10. The 2026-08-03 follow-up (§ 12) replaced the unpaired interval reading with nine paired tile-swap ΔMCC permutation tests (10,000 permutations, seed 42, buffer-invariant, each cross-checked against an exact McNemar test): every point estimate favours the higher temperature, but only the end-to-end T=0.3-vs-T=1.0 contrast is robust (−0.1319 p=0.0005 at N=5, −0.1023 p=0.0023 at N=10; the only two surviving BH over the six pool-matched tests). The adjacent-rung T=0.7-vs-T=1.0 contrast that the disjoint intervals headlined is significant at N=5 (p=0.0255) but NOT at N=10 (p=0.2114) — so the non-overlapping BCa intervals overstated the N=10 evidence, and § 11.2's expectation that they would be conservative for a paired design is withdrawn. Extending the ladder to T=0.0 and T=0.3 shows tile-level MCC rising monotonically with temperature (0.2235 / 0.3129 / 0.3655 / 0.4153 at N=10) via flat sensitivity and climbing specificity, replicating Obs 274's finding on the preregistered Phase 2b sweep; on F1 the entire ladder is non-significant. Honest summary: no reliable matched-scope temperature advantage for T=0.7 at consensus level; on tile-level MCC the advantage runs the other way; and this is not an exception to the project's lower-temperature-is-better pattern, which is an object-level F1 pattern (55-map deployment oracle, T0.3 > T0.7 = +0.020 corrected-F1 @ 50 m, p<0.001) and never an MCC one.

analyses.outcome: PREDICTION SPLIT: the registered MECHANISM is confirmed, the registered PERFORMANCE claim is falsified. F1 falls monotonically as overlap rises - arm A (12.5 %) 0.5578, arm B (25 %) 0.5198, arm C (50 %) 0.4025 (common scope, 20 m, mean of 3 passes). All three paired tile-bootstrap contrasts exclude zero at B = 1,000 and B = 10,000 (A-B +0.0380, CI95 [+0.0009, +0.0708] - marginal; A-C +0.1554 [+0.1214, +0.1889]; B-C +0.1174 [+0.0922, +0.1437]). Recall behaves exactly as registered (0.7379 -> 0.7844 -> 0.8717) but precision falls faster (0.4484 -> 0.3887 -> 0.2616). The registered edge-detection analysis confirms the hypothesised mechanism and localises it: the ten mounds arm A could only ever see within 100 m of a tile edge go from recall 0.2667 (A) to 0.7667 (B) to 0.9333 (C), against 0.7468 -> 0.7847 -> 0.8706 for the other 528; arm A misses all four of the most edge-marooned mounds in all three passes and arm C finds all four. The gain is real but concentrated in under 2 % of mounds, too few to pay for the precision lost elsewhere. Cost-efficiency: every additional API dollar spent on overlap buys NEGATIVE F1 (A->B -0.1011 F1 per additional $; B->C -0.0522; arm A's $1.3708 is imputed at the measured B/C per-call rate, arms B and C are audited spend, $5.7488 total including the smoke test). Tile-level MCC (A 0.106, B 0.258, C 0.059) is NOT robust to the scope choice and carries no overlap claim here.
